name: LeBron James
bio: A four-time champion and the league's all-time leading scorer, LeBron James is a point-forward who initiates offense from the wing. Now in his forties, he plays fewer minutes but still carries the Lakers' half-court creation.

name: Anthony Davis
bio: An elite interior defender and rim protector who anchors the Lakers defense. Davis operates mostly in the paint and from the short mid-range, and his availability has historically been the swing factor in Los Angeles.

name: Austin Reaves
bio: An undrafted guard who became a starter through shot-making and secondary playmaking. Reaves is a connective piece who thrives playing off LeBron James and Anthony Davis.

name: Stephen Curry
bio: The most prolific three-point shooter in basketball history and the engine of Golden State's motion offense. Curry's off-ball gravity reshapes defensive coverages before he ever touches the ball.

name: Draymond Green
bio: A defensive quarterback and hub passer who rarely looks for his own shot. Green's career includes several high-profile suspensions for on-court incidents, and he has been at the center of multiple documented locker room disputes.

name: Jonathan Kuminga
bio: An explosive young forward who attacks downhill and finishes above the rim. Kuminga's fit alongside Golden State's veteran core has been a recurring subject of trade speculation.

name: Kevin Durant
bio: A seven-foot wing scorer with guard skills, widely considered the most efficient shot-maker of his era. Durant has played for four franchises and several of his departures were preceded by publicly reported friction.

name: Devin Booker
bio: A mid-range specialist and primary initiator for Phoenix. Booker's scoring versatility lets him play on or off the ball alongside other high-usage creators.

name: Bradley Beal
bio: A three-level scorer who arrived in Phoenix carrying the league's only full no-trade clause. Beal's contract has been a persistent obstacle in Phoenix's roster construction.

name: Nikola Jokic
bio: A three-time MVP and the most productive passing big man in league history. Drafted in the second round during a fast food commercial break, Jokic runs Denver's offense from the elbow and the post.

name: Jamal Murray
bio: Denver's closer and two-man-game partner with Nikola Jokic. Murray's playoff shot-making has repeatedly exceeded his regular season output.

name: Aaron Gordon
bio: A defensive forward who guards the opposing team's best scorer and finishes lobs from Jokic. Gordon accepted a reduced offensive role after being traded from Orlando.

name: Anthony Edwards
bio: An explosive young wing scorer and the face of Minnesota's rebuild. Edwards combines elite athleticism with an improving pull-up three.

name: Rudy Gobert
bio: A four-time Defensive Player of the Year who protects the rim and never shoots outside the paint. Gobert's arrival in Minnesota was one of the largest trade packages ever surrendered for a single player.

name: Karl-Anthony Towns
bio: A seven-footer who shoots better from three than most guards. Towns moved to power forward to accommodate Rudy Gobert, a pairing that drew heavy skepticism before it worked.

name: Luka Doncic
bio: A high-usage creator who controls tempo through pace manipulation and step-back shooting. Doncic led the league in scoring while carrying one of the highest offensive loads on record.

name: Kyrie Irving
bio: One of the most skilled ball handlers and finishers in league history. Irving has requested trades from multiple franchises, and several of those exits followed publicly reported disagreements with teammates or management.

name: Daniel Gafford
bio: A vertical-spacing rim runner acquired at the trade deadline. Gafford finishes lobs and blocks shots without needing offensive touches.

name: Ja Morant
bio: An explosive downhill guard whose recent seasons have been shortened by suspension and injury. Morant's off-court conduct has repeatedly become a league disciplinary matter.

name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
bio: A former Defensive Player of the Year who blocks shots on the perimeter and at the rim. Jackson's foul rate is the main constraint on his minutes.

name: Desmond Bane
bio: A late-first-round pick who developed into a high-volume shooter and secondary creator. Bane's shooting stroke was considered mechanically unorthodox coming out of college.

name: Jayson Tatum
bio: Boston's primary scorer and a three-level shot creator. Tatum's shot selection and late-game decision-making have been a recurring subject of national debate.

name: Jaylen Brown
bio: A powerful downhill wing and switchable defender who signed the largest contract in league history at the time. Brown's fit next to Jayson Tatum has been questioned by analysts for years.

name: Kristaps Porzingis
bio: A seven-foot-three center who shoots threes and protects the rim. Porzingis has played for four teams, and his first departure from New York was reported to follow a breakdown in his relationship with the front office.

name: Jalen Brunson
bio: An undersized second-round guard who became an All-NBA lead creator in New York. Brunson wins with footwork and pace rather than burst.

name: Julius Randle
bio: A bruising left-handed forward who initiates from the elbow. Randle's relationship with the Madison Square Garden crowd has swung sharply between seasons.

name: OG Anunoby
bio: A switchable perimeter stopper acquired midseason from Toronto. Anunoby guards all five positions and spaces the floor without needing usage.

name: Joel Embiid
bio: A former MVP who scores from the post, the mid-range and the free throw line at historic rates. Embiid's availability has been the defining question of Philadelphia's decade.

name: Tyrese Maxey
bio: A blazing-fast guard who took over lead creation duties in Philadelphia. Maxey's transition speed and pull-up shooting expanded dramatically after James Harden's departure.

name: Paul George
bio: A two-way wing who shoots efficiently off movement and defends on the ball. George has changed franchises three times, each move driven by contract leverage.

name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
bio: A two-time MVP and champion who scores almost entirely at the rim through downhill drives. Antetokounmpo's lack of a jump shot has never meaningfully limited his production.

name: Damian Lillard
bio: A deep-range pull-up shooter who spent eleven seasons in Portland before requesting a trade. Lillard publicly named a single preferred destination and was dealt elsewhere.

name: Brook Lopez
bio: A drop-coverage center who blocks shots at the rim and shoots high-volume threes. Lopez reinvented himself from a back-to-the-basket post scorer in his late twenties.

name: Jimmy Butler
bio: A playoff riser whose regular season output understates his impact. Butler's exits from Chicago, Minnesota and Philadelphia each followed widely reported conflicts with teammates or coaching staff.

name: Bam Adebayo
bio: A switchable center who defends guards on the perimeter and orchestrates from the elbow. Adebayo's lack of a three-point shot is the main critique of his offensive game.

name: Tyler Herro
bio: A movement shooter and secondary creator whose name has appeared in nearly every Miami trade rumor for three straight seasons.

name: Jordan Poole
bio: A high-variance shot creator who was traded to Washington in the summer following a widely reported practice altercation with a Golden State teammate. Poole's shot diet leans heavily on difficult pull-ups.

name: Kyle Anderson
bio: A deliberate, slow-tempo forward nicknamed for his pace, who passes and defends more than he scores. Anderson was at the center of an on-court scuffle that drew one of the longest suspensions of the season for an opposing player.
